summary: Configured node1 to run a chrooted web application as appsvc on port 8080. The systemd service starts at boot and recovered successfully after a verified node restart. RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 remain unchanged.
actions_performed: Built /srv/app-chroot using the installed Python 3.12.9 runtime and compatible system libraries.
Installed and enabled chroot-web.service under multi-user.target.
Verified the process runs as appsvc with /srv/app-chroot as its root and listens on 0.0.0.0:8080.
Restarted node1 safely and verified automatic service recovery and HTTP health.

evidence.requirement: Web application runs inside a chroot as unprivileged appsvc on port 8080
evidence.summary: Process UID/GID is appsvc/992, process root is /srv/app-chroot, port 8080 listens on all interfaces, and /health returns status=ok with uid=992.

evidence.requirement: Application starts at boot without an interactive login
evidence.summary: chroot-web.service is enabled under multi-user.target and became active automatically after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Installed OS release and kernel were retained
evidence.summary: Before and after configuration/reboot, node1 reports RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.

evidence.requirement: Runtime is compatible with the installed platform
evidence.summary: The copied Python 3.12.9 runtime successfully imported the HTTP stack from inside the chroot as UID 992.

Healthy baseline used boot ID e625b9a5-4242-499a-88da-9a76ecf86fe1; reboot was acknowledged; the new boot ID is 5965c679-a6a1-4941-b3b2-18f5624eb276; system state, service, chroot identity, listener, and HTTP response all recovered.
